items.text: COMMITTEE DISCHARGED AND COMMITTED TO RULES

items.actClause:
AN ACT to amend the vehicle and traffic law and the public health law, in
relation to driving a motor vehicle under the influence of drugs or combined
use of drugs and alcohol and defines the term inhalant
items.lawCode: Add §119-c, amd §1192, V & T L; amd §3380, Pub Health L
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S6092

SPONSOR: KAMINSKY
 
TITLE OF BILL:  An act to amend the vehicle and traffic law and the
public health law, in relation to driving a motor vehicle under the
influence of drugs or combined use of drugs and alcohol and defines the
term inhalant

 
PURPOSE:

To expand the definition of driving while ability impaired to include
inhalants and other impairing substances.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1 amends section 119-c of the Vehicle and Traffic law to define
an inhalant.

Section 2 amends section 1192 of the Vehicle and Traffic Law to include
inhalants and other impairing substances to the description of driving
while ability impaired by drugs and the combined offense.

Section 3 amends the public health to expand the definition of hazardous
inhalants.

Section 4 adds a new subdivision to the Vehicle and Traffic law to
create an affirmative defense for operators who suffer medical emergen-
cies.

Section 5 is the effective date.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

The CDC estimates that 130 Americans die every day from an opioid over-
dose. In New York, there were 3,224 opioid-related overdoses. Most of
these deaths were caused by synthetic opioids. In 2017, 2,238 people
died of overdosing on synthetic opioids, which was up from the 210
deaths in 2013. Synthetic drugs also passed prescription opioids as the
most common drugs involved in overdose deaths in the United States.

Increased use of inhalants and synthetic drugs also means people are
more likely to drive while under the influence of these illicit drugs.
According to the National Institute of Drug Abuse, in 2017, 21.4 million
people drove under the influence of alcohol and 12.8 million drove under
the influence of illicit drugs. Further, estimates show that 44% of
drivers in fatal crashes tested positive for drugs. Even with these
facts, experts still find it difficult to calculate how many crashes
occur because an individual is under the influence of drugs, including
synthetic drugs or inhalants.

New York has repeatedly taken steps to keep people safe by removing
intoxicated drivers from the road. Yet our state has failed to update
our laws to include the use of synthetic drugs and inhalants.  Current-
ly, prosecutors do not have the necessary tools to charge drivers who
use these substances with driving while intoxicated even though these
drugs cause impaired motor functions and judgment. It important that our
laws change to address these new drugs so that our courts can properly
prosecute impaired drivers.

 
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

New bill.

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

None.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect on the one hundred eightieth day.
